questions.question: During the first world war (1914 - 1918):
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prices almost doubled.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **World War 1 is also known as the Great War or Global War **was a deadly global conflict that occurred in **Europe that lasted from 28th July 1914 to 11th November 1918****.**
 
• World War 1 is one of the largest wars in history.

**Price effect:**__ The impact that a change in value has on the consumer demand for a product or service in the market. 

__
 
• Industrial prices **nearly doubled in the six years** after 1914 and accelerating prices benefitted the Indian industry.
 
• **Farm prices rose** as well, but at a slower pace than **industrial prices. **The internal terms of trade moved against agriculture.
 
• This trend continued for most of the next few decades, and especially during the collapse in global commodity prices during the **Great Depression.**
 
• The** rapid rise in industrial prices as well as improving internal terms of trade** for Indian industry benefitted industrial enterprises.
 
• World War I took the United States out of a **recession** into a **44-month economic boom.**
 
• **Hyperinflation and unemployment **in Germany were staggering.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• It is widely believed that the assassination of **Archduke Franz Ferdinand and his wife** during a visit to **Serbia is the spark that ignited the conflict** of World War I. 
 
• European powers were divided into 2 groups: **The** Allied Powers** and the** **Central Powers.**
 
• The Allied Powers - **France, Italy, Britain, Russia, and Japan.**
 
• The Central Powers - **Germany, Austria, Hungary, Bulgaria, and the Ottoman Empire.**
 
• World War I ended with the **defeat of the Central Powers.**
 
• **The Treaty of Versailles** was the most important of the peace treaties that brought World War 1 to an end.
 
• The treaty ended with the state of war between Germany and the Allied Powers.

questions.question: The attack by the third estate on the Bastille prison sparked the _______.
questions.solution:
The correct option is **2** i.e.** ​**__**French Revolution**__.

 
• The attack by the third estate on the Bastille State prison took place on **14th July 1789**.
 
• The French revolution **started in 1789 and ended in 1799**.
 
• The motive was the upheaval of the **French monarchy and the poor economic policies of King Louis XVI**.
 
• The ideals of** Liberty, Equality and Fraternity** were added from the French Revolution.

questions.question: When did the epidemic of Black Death (a type of Plague) spread in entire Europe?
questions.solution: Black Death a type of plague spread in the entire Europe during the period of 1346-1353. The plague caused by Yersinia pestis bacterium, killed 50% of European population and created a series of socio religious and economic upheavals in the European continent.

questions.question: In which battle was Napoleon defeated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **3** i.e __**Waterloo**__.

 
• Napoleon Bonaparte was the **Emperor of the French**.

 
 
• He ruled France twice.
 
• The first reign was from 1804 to 1814.
 
• The second reign was in 1815.
 
• He led many successful campaigns during the** French Revolutionary Wars**.
 
• Napoleon Bonaparte is considered one of the greatest commanders in history.
 
• He fought more than 70 battles, losing only seven, mostly at the end.
 
 
 
• Important Battles won by Napoleon Bonaparte are:
 
 
• Battle of Montenotte
 
• Battle of Ceva.
 
• Battle of Lodi.
 
• Battle of Borghetto.
 
• Battle of Mount Tabor.
 
• Battle of Borodino.
 
• **Battle of Arcole** in 1796
 
• **Battle of Jena** in 1806
 
• **Battle of Ligny **in 1815.
 
 
 
• Napoleon was defeated in the Battle of Waterloo.
 
 
• The Battle of Waterloo was fought in **1815 in Belgium**.
 
• Battle fought between Napoleon's French Army and a coalition led by the Duke of Wellington and Marshal Blücher. 
 
• Battle of Waterloo resulted in:
 
 
• End of the Seventh Coalition.
 
• Final defeat of Napoleon.
 
• End of the Napoleonic Wars.

questions.question: Which European country was not one of the signatories of the Treaties of Rome establishing the European Economic Community in 1957?
questions.solution:
• The **Treaty of Rome** established the **European Economic Community** on **25 March 1957. **It is also known as **Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TEFU).**
 
• It was signed by** Italy, France, Belgium, West Germany, and the Netherlands.**
 
• It came into force on **January 1, 1958** and is one of the two treaties that lays the **constitutional basis of European Union.**
 
• The second treaty is** Treaty on European Union (TEU).**

questions.question: In which year was the Treaty of Versailles signed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1919**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Treaty of Versailles **was the most important of **World War I's peace treaties.**
 
• It brought the war **between Germany and the Allies to an end**.
 
• It was signed in the Palace of Versailles on June 28, 1919, exactly five years after Archduke Franz Ferdinand was assassinated, sparking the war.
 
• On the German side, the other Central Powers signed separate treaties. Although the 11 November 1918 armistice halted the war, the peace accord took six months of Allied negotiations at the Paris Peace Conference.
 
• **On October 21, 1919**, the League of Nations Secretariat registered the treaty.
 
• **The Locarno Treaties, **which improved relations between Germany and other European powers, and the re-negotiation of the reparation system, which resulted in the Dawes Plan, the Young Plan, and the indefinite postponement of reparations at the Lausanne Conference of 1932, were the results of the treaty's problems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Treaty of Versailles:**

 Signed: 28 June 1919
 
 
•

• 
 Effective: 10 January 1920
 
 
•

questions.question: The Soviet Union broke down in the year _______.
questions.solution:
The correct option is **1** i.e. __**1991**__.

 
• The Soviet Union was officially known as the **Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR)**.
 
• It was** established in 1922** and lasted till 1991.
 
• It was a group of of **15 Soviet Socialist Republics**.
 
• The Soviet Union has its **origins **in the** Russian Revolution of 1917**.

questions.question: In the middle of the first century BC, under ________, a high-born military commander, the ‘Roman Empire’ was extended to present-day Britain and Germany.
questions.solution:
• In the middle of the first century BC, under **Julius Caesar**, a high-born military commander, the ‘Roman Empire’ was extended to present-day Britain and Germany. 
 
• He was a **historian, a military general, and a Roman politician** who played a major role in the events that led to the rise of the Roman Empire and demise of the Roman Republic.

questions.question: During 1850’s, Britain came to be known as _________.
questions.solution: During 1850’s, Britain came to be known as the workshop of the world since it became the leading industrial nation in the 19th century because of its mechanised manufacturing of cotton textiles and also the growth of its iron and steel industries in the 1850s.

questions.question: The Great Leap Forward (GLF) was a campaign initiated in ______ in 1958 aimed at industrialising the country on a massive scale.

• It was aimed to **modernize China's economy. **

questions.question: In which of the following states has a commemorative pillar for Polish refugee families, that made India their home during World War II, been set up?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **A pillar in remembrance of World War II** Polish fugitives was disclosed in** Maharashtra Village.**
 
• As their country was destroyed by invading armies, **around 5,000 refugees** from Poland lived at** Valivade, 235 km from Pune, between 1942 and 1948.**
 
• Throughout World War II, thousands of Poles fled their country and looked for** refuge around the world.**
 
• One of the first countries to support was **India,** beginning with the so-called** "Good Maharaja' Jam Saheb, who took in many Polish orphans.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **​**Hitler's attack on Poland in **September 1939** drove Great Britain and France to announce war on Germany, starting **World War II.**
 
• World War II or the Second World War, often abbreviated as WW II, was a **worldwide war that lasted from 1939 to 1945. **
 
• The Second World War started on September **1, 1939 with Hitler's attack on Poland** and ended with the **Japanese surrender on **September **2, 1945**.** **

questions.question: The French Revolution, a period that brought far-reaching social and political upheaval in France, began in _________.
questions.solution: The French Revolution was a period of far-reaching social and political upheaval in France that lasted from 1789 to 1799. The Revolution overthrew the monarchy and established a liberal and republic government.

questions.question: The United States of America adopted a democratic constitution in _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **2 **i.e __**1787**__.

 
• The Constitution of the United States is the supreme law of the United States of America.
 
 
• The United States of America adopted a democratic constitution in **1787**.
 
• Constitution of America came into force in **1789**.
 
• '**We the People**' are the first three words of the American constitution.
 
• American constitution has been amended **27 times**.
 
• The first ten amendments are collectively known as the **Bill of Rights**.
 
• The Continental Congress functioned as the provisional government of the United States From 1774 to 1781.
 
 
 
• Important features of the American constitution are:
 
 
• Judicial review
 
• Preamble
 
• Fundamental Rights
 
• Impeachment
